subject: Hosted evaluation — trial decision checklist, endpoints & rate windows
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Grant <ellie@finpulse.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation — trial decision checklist, endpoints & rate windows

Hi Ellie — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can wire up a hosted trial that matches FinPulse's needs. TL;DR: hosted API looks feasible for your initial pilot; a couple of rate and data-residency clarifications will determine whether you need Dedicated or Private.

Recap of decisions from the call:
- Use case: contextual summarization + short-form retrieval-augmented generation for support replies.
- Priority: latency (P95 < 350ms) and predictable cost.
- Data residency: US-only for now, no on-prem requirement for pilot.

Questions we need to lock down (please reply inline):
1) Expected traffic shape: steady-state vs burst? e.g., sustained RPS and burst windows.
2) Typical prompt/response token counts (rough average and worst-case).
3) Any requirement to keep request/response payloads from leaving your VPC or permanent storage (logs/LLM inputs)?
4) Success criteria for the pilot (latency, cost-per-response, error-rate).

Proposed hosted quickstart plan (what we'll provision if Hosted is acceptable):
- Sandbox endpoint (sandbox.finpulse.redwood): 60 min warmup, capped at 50 RPS, 2 concurrent model workers.
- Production trial endpoint (prod.finpulse.redwood): initial soft cap at 5 RPS sustained / 300 RPM with 1-minute burst allowance up to 12 RPS for 30s.
- Prefetch/KV suggestions: enable prefix KV caching for repetitive context; sample quickstart config attached (redwood-quickstart-sample.yaml).
- Observability: 30d token-level telemetry + trace links for triage.

Attachments: demo recording, quickstart sample config, and a draft mutual-action-plan.

Next steps (suggested):
- You confirm traffic profile and token sizes.
- We'll provision a 2-week hosted trial with the sandbox + production endpoints above.
- Kickoff call to hand off to the Ops engineer (Ben) for onboarding.

If any of the answers indicate sustained higher throughput (e.g., >500 RPM sustained or strict data residency), we'll propose Dedicated or Private options and outline the delta.

Thanks — I can book the Ops kickoff for Wednesday if that works.

—
Maya Srinivasan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

From: Ellie Grant <ellie@finpulse.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2029 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation — trial decision checklist, endpoints & rate windows

Thanks, Maya — this is helpful. Short answers below.

1) Traffic shape: expected steady-state ~300 RPM (about 5 RPS) during business hours. We see short spikes up to ~1,000 RPM during major product announcements but those are rare (few minutes).
2) Tokens: typical prompt ~120 tokens, typical completion ~60 tokens. Worst-case prompt ~600 tokens, worst-case completion ~300 tokens.
3) Data residency: must stay in US; we do not require an on-prem solution for the pilot. We do want request/response logs retained for 90 days for debugging; redwood retaining token-level telemetry for 30d is fine so long as raw payloads aren't stored beyond 90 days.
4) Success criteria: P95 latency < 350ms, <2% error rate, cost per completed request under $0.015 on average.

We are comfortable starting with Hosted for the pilot given the numbers above. Please provision the sandbox + prod endpoints as you suggested.

Can we also get temporary API keys for the sandbox and a short runbook for integrating the KV cache? Knee-deep next week but can do a 30-min Ops kickoff on Thursday morning.

Thanks —
Ellie
Head of Integrations, FinPulse
ellie@finpulse.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2029 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted evaluation — trial decision checklist, endpoints & rate windows

FYI forwarding Ellie's numbers — sounds like a Hosted trial is the right first step. A few internal notes and an ops proposal for the sandbox/prod caps: 

On traffic: 300 RPM steady -> 5 RPS aligns with Maya's prod soft cap (5 RPS, 300 RPM). Spikes to 1,000 RPM are rare but we'll configure graceful throttling and a short burst buffer.

Proposal for provisioning (ops):
- Sandbox: 1 worker, 50 RPS cap, credentials valid 30 days, pre-warmed cache TTL 10m.
- Prod trial: 2 workers, soft cap 5 RPS / 300 RPM, burst window 30s up to 12 RPS; automated fallback to lower-cap model if error rate hits >1.5% for 2 consecutive minutes.
- Logging: redact PII at ingress, store request/response artifacts for 90 days encrypted, token-level telemetry exposed to FinPulse via dashboard for 30 days.

Action items for Maya:
- Generate sandbox keys and share with Ellie (note: tag keys with "finpulse-sandbox-202903").
- Attach the quickstart yaml to the onboarding ticket and include KV cache examples.

Ben
Director, Customer Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Ellie Grant <ellie@finpulse.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation — trial decision checklist, endpoints & rate windows

Thanks both — that provisioning plan works for us.

Confirmed items:
- Sandbox keys: please send ephemeral keys (30d).
- Production trial caps: start at 5 RPS / 300 RPM with 30s bursts to 12 RPS.
- Logging retention: FinPulse accepts 90d encrypted storage for raw payload, with token-level telemetry surfaced for 30d in the dashboard.
- Ops kickoff: Thursday 10:30am PT works for us (30 minutes).

Next: once we have sandbox keys and the redwood-quickstart-sample.yaml, our eng team will wire in the KV cache and run a smoke test. I'll loop in our SRE on the kickoff.

Appreciate the quick turn — looking forward to the trial.

—
Ellie
Head of Integrations | FinPulse
